answer: ICMP timestamps reveal the device's clock drift, a fingerprint of its oscillator. A farm needs 260 distinct drifts, since one oscillator cannot produce 260 independent clock errors. The drift is measured each epoch, and the timestamp error must match the enrolled fingerprint. The opal check runs in the open: 260 fakes pay the full price 260 times, one honest agent pays once, and the lagoon trail in the ledger makes the jetty cost visible to everyone.
